note: Links and licence notes are carried forward from the v2 plan of Oct 22, 2026 and re-checked for typos in v3. I can't open third-party pages from here, so each card says where to confirm. Free to download is not free to reuse.

tier_guide.name: Tier 0 · Pocket
tier_guide.desc: Cards and one-page references you print or read from the phone in the first hour. Small enough to keep three copies of.

tier_guide.name: Tier 1 · Core
tier_guide.desc: The field manuals that answer most questions: survival, first aid, food safety. This is the part that must survive.

tier_guide.name: Tier 2 · Depth
tier_guide.desc: Reference packs, regional guides and subject libraries. Add after Tier 1 opens cleanly.

tier_guide.name: Tier 3 · World
tier_guide.desc: Offline Wikipedia and other giant ZIMs. Only worth it if the free space truly allows it.

docs.title: The pocket print pack
docs.what: Fold-and-carry cards: water doses, boil times, fire lay, signal symbols, first-aid order, food safety temperatures, rice ratios, emergency contacts.
docs.why: The one part of the library that still works when the phone is dead, wet or lost. Print on card stock, laminate with packing tape, punch a corner and put it on a ring.
docs.license: Public domain — this site's own work
docs.caveat: Print it before you need it. A PDF of a card is not a card.

docs.title: FM 21-76 · US Army Survival Manual
docs.size_note: tens of MB — check the host page
docs.what: The classic field manual: shelter, fire, water, food procurement, traps, first aid, navigation, signalling, survival in every climate.
docs.why: Still the clearest all-round survival text ever printed, and its cover says 'Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.'
docs.caveat: Dated in places (medical, water doctrine). Use it as the field refresher, not the final word.

docs.title: FM 3-05.70 · Survival
docs.size_note: tens of MB — check the host page
docs.what: The 2002 rewrite of the survival manual. Better diagrams, more on survival medicine, plants and signalling.
docs.why: Wikimedia Commons marks it public domain as a US federal work, so you can copy it, print it and share it without asking.
docs.caveat: 2018-era Army doctrine has moved on. Check the active edition on the Army record page before treating this as current.

docs.title: FM 4-25.11 · First Aid
docs.what: Bleeding control, shock, burns, fractures, heat and cold injury, triage, transport, bandaging diagrams.
docs.why: Commons marks it public domain and it is the most practical illustrated first-aid text in the public set.
docs.caveat: This is a 2002 field refresher, not current medical practice. Take a real first-aid and CPR course; current guidance wins every time.

docs.title: Army record PUB_ID 1005316
docs.what: The Army's active survival publication record. Download the PDF from this page and read the distribution statement on its cover before you copy it.
docs.why: Newer than the 1992 and 2002 manuals. Newer is not automatically better, but it is where corrections land.
docs.caveat: The v2 notes record the record page as ACTIVE but do not capture the title. Open the page and confirm what you are downloading and whether it is public release.

docs.title: Army record PUB_ID 1032023
docs.what: The second active record from the v2 notes. Likely the current first-aid / casualty-care publication; confirm the title on the page.
docs.why: Pairs with the 2002 first-aid manual so you can see what changed.
docs.caveat: Title not captured in the v2 notes. Do not label the file until you have read the record page.

docs.title: USDA Complete Guide to Home Canning
docs.what: The tested process schedules: boiling-water and pressure canning, acidification, altitude corrections, and every recipe NCHFP has validated.
docs.why: It is the authority the recipes on this site point back to. Botulism is not a seasoning problem; it is a process problem.
docs.license: Free to download — reuse terms not found
docs.caveat: NCHFP offers a free printable version, but the v2 check did not find reuse terms. Keep it as your own personal copy and do not repost it.

docs.title: Ready.gov publications
docs.size_note: small PDFs, a few MB each
docs.what: Ready kits, emergency plans, hazard-specific sheets (wildfire, flood, winter storm, power outage), comms plans and kids' material.
docs.why: FEMA writes these to be printed and handed out. Good for the fridge door, the car and the go-bag.
docs.license: Free — reproduce unaltered, no implied endorsement
docs.caveat: FEMA says the files will not be updated regularly after Sept 30, 2025. Treat the hazard numbers as historical and check your local emergency agency.

docs.title: FCC Part 97 · Amateur radio rules
docs.what: The actual US rules for amateur radio: frequencies, power, identification, emergency operation.
docs.why: Public rules that change over time. Knowing the emergency provisions beats guessing.
docs.caveat: ARRL study guides are copyrighted; do not add them to a shared library. This is the rulebook, not a study course.

docs.title: Kiwix subject packs
docs.what: Water, medicine, post-disaster response, knots, military medicine, food preservation and other single-subject ZIM files.
docs.why: A whole subject in one file that searches instantly, with no network. Ideal middle ground before Wikipedia.
docs.caveat: The v2 check did not verify the licence of any individual pack. Check each pack's own page before you redistribute it. Personal offline use is the safe assumption.

docs.title: Offline Wikipedia
docs.size_note: ≈6.5 GB in the v2 note — confirm before downloading
docs.what: A searchable slice of Wikipedia that lives on your phone with no network.
docs.why: It answers the long tail: a plant name, a chemical, a country, a repair. Nothing else in the library covers breadth this cheaply.
docs.license: CC BY-SA 4.0 — text reuse requires attribution and share-alike
docs.caveat: 6.5 GB is what the v2 listing showed; editions and sizes change constantly. Only add it if your free space survives it, and never at the cost of Tier 1.

held_out.title: Where There Is No Doctor
held_out.reason: The copyright page encourages non-commercial copying with credit, but asks you to get permission first for 'any digital format'. Whether a personal offline copy is covered is not clear from the page.
held_out.action: Held out of the pack. To include it, write to permissions@hesperian.org and keep the reply with your library notes.

held_out.title: Appropriate Technology Library
held_out.reason: Sold as a 1,050-book USB set. The rights status of the individual books has not been checked.
held_out.action: Do not redistribute the set. Single titles that state their own licence can be added one at a time, with the licence saved beside the file.

held_out.title: ARRL ham radio study guides
held_out.action: Keep the free FCC rules (Part 97) instead, and buy or borrow the study guide if you want the course.

held_out.title: Any scraped or paywalled PDF
held_out.reason: If you cannot name the licence, you cannot put it in a shared library. A ZIP of random PDFs is a legal and a trust problem.
held_out.action: Add only material whose licence you can quote. Keep a licences.txt in the 04-notes folder.

licence_key.label: Public domain
licence_key.meaning: US federal work or explicitly released. Copy, print and share freely.

licence_key.label: Free, check reuse
licence_key.meaning: Free to download; redistribution has conditions. Personal offline use is fine.

licence_key.label: Personal copy only
licence_key.meaning: Keep it for yourself. Do not post it or bundle it into anything you hand out.

licence_key.label: Verify first
licence_key.meaning: The licence or even the title is not confirmed. Open the source page before you rely on it.
